LESSON: WRITING PRACTICE

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: Writing
Topic 3.2: Writing Practice
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 5

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing Practice, part of Writing in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: What do you do to make a three letter word?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. recall letters of the alphabet in the right sequence,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing Practice in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.

B. write syllables by joining consonants and vowels,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing Practice in the Kenya CBC curriculum.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing Practice together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
• Social justice: The learner chants rhymes on letter sounds while working with others and sharing the opportunity to do so

equitably.

• Integrity: The learner writes own work even in the absence of teacher with honesty and accountability.

Core Competencies:

• Self-efficacy: The learner correctly and confidently reads and writes three letter words by joining syllables and sounds and

displays in class work done.

• Critical thinking and problem solving: The learner differentiates between lower and upper case, letters while writing them

down in books.

Values:

• Social justice: The learner chants rhymes on letter sounds while working with others and sharing the opportunity to do so

equitably.

• Integrity: The learner writes own work even in the absence of teacher with honesty and accountability.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issue(
s) :

Personal hygiene awareness: The learner clears the working area and washes hands with soap and water.

Link to other Activity Areas: Pattern writing links to Creative Activities where the learners make different patterns.

Suggested learning resources: plasticine, modeling clay, adapted pencils, page turners, audio books, book holders, flash

cards
